item.title: Policy support buoys full-year growth outlook
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Policy support buoys full-year growth outlook Nation offers opportunities, confidence to foreign firms amid global uncertainty China is right on track to meet its full-year economic growth goal as stepped-up policy efforts bolster domestic demand, with sustained growth offering opportunities for foreign businesses amid global economic uncertainty, experts and executives said. The latest measures, which are targeted in nature, signal a higher priority for stabilizing growth by boosting infrastructure investment, stabilizing the property market and improving people's livelihoods, with ample scope for additional support in the fourth quarter, they said. Their comments came after Finance Minister Lan Fo'an pledged to ensure existing policies deliver results and devise targeted additional measures to help achieve annual development goals, in an article for Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. "We will place greater emphasis on expanding domestic effective demand to maintain stable economic operation," Lan said in the article, which was posted on the Ministry of Finance's website on Thursday. He called for coordinating government bond funding to support infrastructure and major projects and tapping the unused portion of local government debt limits to strengthen local budgets and investment. Lan's remarks, together with the recent rollout of targeted stimulus measures, underscore policymakers' commitment to delivering steady growth and strengthening investor confidence, analysts said. On Tuesday, the ministry, together with other departments, rolled out mortgage subsidies for eligible homebuyers to ease their burden and support essential housing needs. The People's Bank of China, the country's central bank, also on Tuesday cut the one-year rate on pledged supplemental lending — an instrument for providing large-scale targeted funding — by 0.25 percentage points and expanded its coverage to six infrastructure networks, including computing and next-generation communications, to strengthen support for relevant investment. "Overall, growth stabilization has been given higher priority to address the economic slowdown since the second quarter," said Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank. Wen said that economic momentum may strengthen in the fourth quarter, with infrastructure and manufacturing investment to accelerate and support credit expansion, while mortgage subsidies help underpin housing demand. Stronger growth impetus in September and Tuesday's policy package should help China achieve GDP growth of at least 4.5 percent this year, said Xiong Yuan, chief economist at Guosheng Securities, meeting the annual growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent. The official manufacturing purchasing managers' index, or PMI, rose to 50.1 in September from August's 49.8, ending two months of contraction, the National Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday, indicating that manufacturing activity has resumed expansion as stimulus measures took effect. The outlook comes amid overseas market volatility. US stocks reversed early losses to close higher on Thursday, while US Federal Reserve officials offered differing views on further interest rate increases. Amid global economic uncertainty, international organizations and foreign companies see China's relatively stable growth and pursuit of high-quality development as sources of confidence and opportunity. The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office, or AMRO, projects that China's economy will maintain stable growth at 4.5 percent in both 2026 and 2027, supported by resilient exports and fiscal measures. Achim Loeffler, global business leader of Gore-Tex, said China is the US performance materials manufacturer's fastest-growing market, driven by rising demand for high-performance products across outdoor, urban and lifestyle settings. As a testament to global businesses' confidence in the Chinese economy, equity-based foreign direct investment reached $63.8 billion in the first half, up 55 percent year-on-year, according to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. This included a net increase of $43.1 billion in capital, reflecting long-term investment intentions. Foreign companies' reinvested earnings in China rose 31 percent year-on-year as they devoted more earnings to expanding their operations in the country, SAFE said. Xu Shaofeng, senior vice-president of French conglomerate Schneider Electric, highlighted opportunities from industrial upgrading. "Whether it is equipment renewals, energy conservation and carbon reduction, or artificial intelligence-driven digital transformation, these all place higher demands on specialized services," Xu said. Nevertheless, analysts said faster policy implementation and additional support remain key to achieving the full-year growth target. Yi Huan, chief macroeconomist at Huatai Securities, said increasing the pledged supplemental lending quota would be key to supporting additional bank lending for infrastructure and accelerating project construction. Wang Qing, chief macroeconomic analyst at Orient Golden Credit Rating International, estimated that tapping the unused local debt quotas could enable about 700 billion yuan ($104 billion) in additional government bond issuance. Interest rate and reserve requirement ratio cuts remain possible if needed, he said. Contact the writers at zhoulanxv@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: World's tallest tower for gauging wind completed
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
World's tallest tower for gauging wind completed Deep in the wind-swept expanses of Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, a 360-meter wind measurement tower has become fully operational, marking a new milestone in the country's drive to advance next-generation renewable energy infrastructure. Standing taller than the Eiffel Tower, the structure is the tallest of its kind in the global wind power industry. It anchors an 800-megawatt experimental wind farm in Mulei Kazak autonomous county, according to the Urumqi-headquartered National Technology Innovation Center for Wind Power, which operates the facility. Designed to capture complex high-altitude atmospheric data, the tower conducts gradient observations of wind speed, direction, shear and turbulence intensity at various heights. Zhang Ziping, executive deputy general manager of the center's corporate entity, said the data collected will assist in high-altitude wind energy research and provide a verification basis for designing large-scale wind turbines and building a new-type power system. As manufacturers push to build larger and higher-capacity turbines to capture the stronger and steadier winds found higher in the atmosphere, engineers require precise data that traditional ground-level weather stations are unable to provide. The tower, which was completed on Sept 17, combined with turbine wake monitoring systems and a network of lidar sensors, will create a comprehensive observation network. Industry experts say it will offer a standardized experimental site for formulating and revising China's wind power standards. "The tower's completion will significantly enhance China's capabilities in high-altitude wind resource observation, testing and verification," Zhang said. Also on Sept 17, the center for wind power signed agreements with 11 wind measurement equipment manufacturers and six universities to deepen cooperation between industry and academia. The completion of the massive measurement tower highlights Xinjiang's rapid transformation into a colossal hub for renewable power. Capitalizing on average annual wind speeds of up to 8.2 meters per second and over 1,700 hours of effective sunlight, Mulei county has attracted more than 60 new energy enterprises. In late 2024, it became Xinjiang's first county-level 10-million-kilowatt new energy base, with its grid-connected capacity exceeding 20 million kilowatts by the end of 2025. Li Fengping, head of the county's bureau of commerce, science and technology, and industry and information technology, said Mulei will continue optimizing its business environment and welcomes further cooperation with enterprises, research institutions, universities and industry organizations. Local officials say the county has established a complete supply chain, encompassing everything from wind turbines and blades to photovoltaic modules and energy storage equipment. Across Xinjiang, the clean energy transition is accelerating. According to State Grid Xinjiang Electric Power Co, grid-connected new energy generation hit 89.3 billion kilowatt-hours in the first half of the year — comprising more than 30 percent of total regional power generation. By the end of June, the region's total installed power grid capacity exceeded 267 gigawatts, with new energy accounting for 65 percent. Contact the writers at fangaiqing@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: 5.1m-yuan suborbital space tour listed on Trip.com
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
5.1m-yuan suborbital space tour listed on Trip.com Chinese travel group Trip.com has listed a 5.1 million yuan ($760,000) suborbital space tourism package on its platform, marking a direct effort by Western commercial space operators to tap high-net-worth travelers in China. The six-day luxury itinerary, which was revealed in mid-September, is offered through HHtravel, Trip.com's high-end customized tour subsidiary, in partnership with spaceflight company Virgin Galactic, headquartered in the United States. In the package, clients will undergo three days of preflight training at Spaceport America near Las Cruces, New Mexico. On the fifth day, passengers board Virgin Galactic's air-launched spacecraft for a 90-minute suborbital flight, experiencing several minutes of weightlessness and views of the curvature of the Earth. The package price covers preflight training, ground transport, luxury accommodation in the US, custom spacesuits and commemorative flight footage. However, travelers must separately purchase round-trip flights to the US, specialized personal spaceflight insurance and their visas. The listing has generated robust discussion across Chinese social media regarding high-end consumer spending and spaceflight safety, though industry analysts stress the actual addressable market remains extremely restricted. "The product serves a very niche global segment," said Wei Changren, founder of tourism financial news platform btiii.com, noting that buyers require exceptional physical health, high risk tolerance and substantial liquid wealth. Li Xing, a Beijing-based extreme sports enthusiast, said that while the package offers a rare adventure for ordinary citizens without formal astronaut training, the price remains prohibitive for most consumers. "If I were rich enough, I would register for the trip, but it's much too expensive for me," he said. Wei said the prospect of affordable space tourism could arise in the future. "China has matured its rocket launch technology and space exploration in recent decades," he said. Earlier this year, Beijing-based technology startup InterstellOr, which focuses on commercial manned spacecraft research, announced it will launch a suborbital space trip around 2028. Chen Xu, a senior manager from InterstellOr, told Xinhua News Agency in a recent interview that the requirements for passengers for suborbital tours are not as strict as those for professionally trained astronauts. "The passengers should not have risks of cardiovascular diseases or movement disorders, while having regular vestibular and circulatory functions," Chen told Xinhua, adding that preflight training for such suborbital tours is to develop qualified space travelers rather than a "knockout competition". In 2025, the China National Space Administration unveiled a three-year action plan encouraging high-quality and safe development of the commercial space industry, including space resource utilization and space tourism. Virgin Galactic made its first commercial suborbital spaceflight on June 29, 2023, and has since carried 23 paying customers. chengsi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: China claims first men's football medal in 28 years
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
China defeats Uzbekistan at the Asian Games, ending 28-year medal drought China defeated Uzbekistan 4-3 on penalties after a 2-2 draw on Saturday to claim the men's football bronze medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, ending a 28-year wait for a place on the podium. Goalkeeper Li Hao was the hero in the shootout at Toyota Stadium, saving two penalties to help China secure its fourth Asian Games medal in men's football. China had previously won bronze in 1978, silver in 1994, and bronze in 1998. It was also China's first medal in the event since the men's tournament introduced an under-23 age limit at the 2002 Busan Asian Games. China made a fast start, taking the lead in the 15th minute. Hu Hetao exchanged passes with Kuai Jiwen before breaking into the box and finishing to put China ahead. Uzbekistan, fielding a side without any over-age players, gradually took control of the game and equalized in the 42rd minute through Sardorbek Bakhromov, who finished a combination move with a low shot into the far corner. China regained the lead eight minutes after the restart. Wang Yudong received a pass before cutting a right-footed shot into the top corner from the edge of the box. China came close to extending its advantage when Zhang Yuning struck the post, but Uzbekistan continued to press for an equalizer. The Uzbek side finally leveled in the 89th minute. Li Hao saved the initial effort, but Shodiyor Shodiboyev followed up to score after a lengthy VAR review confirmed the goal. With no extra time in the bronze-medal match, the game went directly to a penalty shootout. Li then made two saves as China prevailed 4-3 to secure the bronze. China had lost 2-1 to South Korea in the semifinals, missing the chance to reach the final as it did at the 1994 Hiroshima Asian Games. After the semifinal defeat, however, head coach Antonio Puche and his players emphasized their determination to fight for a medal. Puche said the bronze was a significant reward for a group of young players. "The match was very tough for both teams," Puche said after the match. "I have to say congratulations to the Uzbekistan team because they fought until the very last second. But we got our medal, and in this moment I am the happiest coach in the world." "These players have a fantastic future. We need to work, we need to push them because we have players with big quality and big heart. This is very important in football," he added. Puche also highlighted China's progress this year. "This year was unbelievable," he said. "To get second place in Saudi Arabia in the under-23 Asian Cup, and now the third place, is unbelievable." China had also defeated Uzbekistan on penalties at the AFC U23 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January. The two sides drew 0-0 after extra time in the quarterfinals before China prevailed 4-2 in the shootout, with Li Hao saving one of Uzbekistan's penalties. It was China's first-ever appearance in the semifinals of the tournament. Puche said China had also prepared specifically for penalty shootouts, practicing them regularly in training. Uzbekistan coach Ravshan Khaydarov said his team controlled much of the game, but was unable to prevail from the spot. "This is the second time we lost on penalties. It's hard to speak about it," Khaydarov said. "Regarding the game, we controlled all of the first half and second half, but we lost on penalties." For China, the bronze ended a long wait for an Asian Games medal and gave the team a place on the podium for the first time since 1998.

item.title: Lingering Garden, Suzhou
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
One of China's four famous classical gardens, Lingering Garden was first built in 1593 during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and is regarded as a masterpiece of garden art in Jiangnan (the southern regions of the lower reaches of the Yangtze River). Its elegant layout combines graceful pavilions, winding covered walkways, tranquil waters, and striking rockeries. Within a compact space, the garden evokes an expansive natural landscape, capturing the classical ideal of finding the beauty of mountains and forests within an urban setting. As you wander through the garden, the scenery unfolds with every step. Architecture and nature blend seamlessly, revealing the refined charm and timeless elegance of Suzhou's classical gardens. www.chinabound.cn Travel with ease in China, and with meaning.

item.title: A little martial arts star in the countryside of Anhui
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
In 2021, Armin Schober, an Austrian, and his wife Huang Qiong took their daughter Alina on a trip to Yixian county, Huangshan city, Anhui province. Captivated by its beautiful natural scenery, rich cultural heritage, and distinctive local architecture, they decided to put down roots there. The couple took over a guesthouse in Tachuan village and named it Alina's Garden. In the idyllic countryside of southern Anhui, Alina is growing up carefree, her days filled with freedom and fun. She runs through the fields with her local friends, chatting about the cartoons and movies they love. In her spare time, she practices martial arts. Her parents hired a martial arts master, and she trains under the instructor for two and a half hours every day without fail. According to her mother, Huang, martial arts have brought Alina closer to Chinese culture and become part of her daily life. Growing up in a multicultural family, Alina is fluent in both Chinese and English. She often helps her parents host visitors from around the world, serving as a bridge between China and the wider world. During the 2026 World Mayors Dialogue in Huangshan, held in late May, she and her parents welcomed international guests. She performed martial arts and Huangmei opera, earning round after round of applause.

item.title: Bite-sized drama boom
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Bite-sized drama boom A fast-growing format is finding audiences across borders When Kevin Chen, a 24-year-old blogger-turned-actor from Penang, Malaysia, was invited to play a leading role in The Lady from the Northeast, curiosity was part of what drew him in. Chinese micro-dramas had already become familiar entertainment among his acquaintances back home. "Nowadays, many of my friends in Malaysia really enjoy watching Chinese micro-dramas," Chen said. "Perhaps because everyone's pace of life is getting faster and faster, micro-dramas can be finished in a comparatively short time, making them very suitable for passing short periods of time." Widely believed to have emerged in 2018 before entering a period of explosive growth from 2022, micro-dramas — usually shot vertically, with episodes lasting just a few minutes — have rapidly become one of China's most popular entertainment formats, both at home and overseas. According to China's National Radio and Television Administration, the number of micro-drama users nationwide has exceeded 800 million, roughly 57 percent of China's population. In the first eight months of 2026, 430,000 micro-dramas went online, 13 times the total for all of 2025. Market growth has been just as striking. In 2025, the sector's market size surpassed 100 billion yuan ($14.9 billion), nearly double the 50.4 billion yuan recorded in 2024 — the year when micro-drama revenue first exceeded the total box-office revenue of films released in domestic theaters. Growing popularity at home has been accompanied by rising interest overseas. "The world is paying great attention to Chinese audiovisual works. Chinese micro-dramas have become a literary and artistic genre fancied by international audiences," He Biao, vice-minister of the National Radio and Television Administration, said at a State Council Information Office briefing in late September. DataEye, a data analytics and research company, has found that monthly active users of micro-drama apps in overseas markets reached 258 million in mid-2026. It forecasts the overseas micro-drama market will exceed $6 billion in 2026, with AI-generated dramas and animated dramas accounting for more than $4 billion, or nearly 70 percent of the total. Lin Qiwen, vice-president of DataEye, said that the United States, Japan and Canada ranked as the top three markets by in-app purchase revenue for overseas micro-drama apps from January to July this year, together accounting for nearly half of the total. Audience tastes also vary by market. "For American audiences, stories with strong female leads are among the most popular," Lin said. For example, a story about a young woman who loses everything, rises again and regains control within a wealthy family would appeal to American audiences. In Southeast Asia, however, romances set in ancient China or stories centered on family tensions — such as conflicts between a woman and her mother-in-law — may have greater appeal, he explained. Those differences have also shaped production models. Chinese micro-dramas distributed in Southeast Asia can often be translated and subtitled, but those targeting Western markets generally require greater localization. "Southeast Asian countries share cultural similarities with China, but for American and European audiences, Chinese companies usually hire locals to remake the scripts while letting Chinese teams be in charge of the formats — after all, the Chinese side has more experience in boosting streaming traffic," Lin said. As Chinese companies pursue wider markets, emerging economies have also shown growing interest in downloading Chinese apps for micro-drama viewing. India, Indonesia and Brazil ranked among the top three markets, accounting for 21.5 percent, 19.4 percent and 9.4 percent, respectively, in the first seven months of this year, according to DataEye.

item.title: Sojourn living fast growing new sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Sojourn living fast growing new sector Searches for sojourn living by overseas users rose 68.17% year-on-year so far For Joseph Henry Stern of the United States, getting to know southwestern China has meant trekking with locals into the mountains to pick mushrooms and learning what to put on his own dinner table. Known locally as "Master Qiao", Stern has settled into a quiet daily rhythm in Yuxi, Yunnan province. Red amaranth, pumpkin shoots and zhe'ergen — a pungent indigenous herb — have become part of his discoveries. He has even learned to make a salad with the herb. "Life here is comfortable and relaxed, and nature is always close at hand," he told local media outlets. That desire to swap a whirlwind itinerary for an authentic daily routine is reshaping China's travel industry. Once dominated by retirees escaping harsh northern winters, sojourn living is expanding across generations. Working-age professionals, digital nomads and multigenerational families are moving into local communities for weeks or months at a time, turning regular neighborhoods and farming villages into vibrant lifestyle hubs. The sharpest acceleration in demand is coming from overseas. According to data provided to China Daily by Trip.com Group, searches for sojourn living by overseas users rose 68.17 percent year-on-year in 2026 to date, far outstripping the 4.88 percent among domestic users. Liu Yanhang, the group's sojourn living research analyst, attributed the growing interest to China's expansion of visa-free policies, streamlined entry procedures, online exposure to Chinese destinations and strong value for money. Widening visa exemptions — including stays of up to 30 days for eligible travelers — give visitors more room to try a slower, immersive itinerary. Shanghai, Beijing, and Guangdong province's Guangzhou and Shenzhen feature among Trip.com's leading destinations for overseas long-stay bookings. Liu said these locations serve a mixture of business trips, family visits and urban exploration. Interest is also spreading beyond those gateways. Dali, Honghe and Baoshan in Yunnan were among destinations recording strong growth in overseas searches, alongside Guangzhou, Chengdu in Sichuan province and Changsha in Hunan province. For international visitors, stays are often modest in length. Seven-day stays account for about 40 percent of overseas long-stay bookings, while roughly a quarter extend to at least 10 days, Liu said. The wider market opportunity is substantial. The China Tourism Academy estimates potential domestic demand at about 600 million trips and a market approaching 3 trillion yuan ($447.3 billion). Policy is encouraging the expansion. A work plan issued by the General Office of the State Council in January designated sojourn tourism services among national priorities for expanding services consumption, calling for upgrades to rural infrastructure, destination services and living facilities. The same desire to participate in everyday life is reshaping the domestic market, where the familiar image of a retiree escaping winter captures only part of the business. Travelers aged 35 to 49 account for about 40 percent of Trip.com's sojourn living customer base, the largest age group, Liu said. Those aged 50 and above make up roughly 12 percent, a share that has remained relatively stable. Among younger and middle-aged customers, including digital nomads and remote workers, Liu described a pattern of combining work and travel: shorter, more frequent stays, movement between destinations and repeat visits. Project schedules and remote-working arrangements help determine how long they can remain. Major cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu, and Hangzhou in Zhejiang appeal for their connections and daily conveniences. Older travelers tend to make fewer moves and stay longer. Climate comes first, followed by living costs, transport and access to medical care. For these customers, a community can matter as much as a room: calligraphy classes, exercise sessions and local cultural activities help fill the weeks. Trip.com's products for active older travelers reflect those priorities. Alongside stays of at least seven days, they include breakfast, shared kitchens and laundry facilities, housekeeping and activities, with health support such as blood-pressure monitoring. In Jinghong, Yunnan, retiree Ao Liming told Economic Daily that members of his community choir had returned to their hometowns but would come back months later. He planned to stay, practicing calligraphy and taking hikes. Such recurring communities give seasonal residents a reason to return beyond the weather. Summer adds another customer configuration — grandparents and grandchildren escaping the heat while working parents remain at home. Tujia, a leading homestay and vacation rental platform, said bookings for stays of at least seven days rose 21 percent during the 2026 summer holiday, while those lasting at least 15 days increased about 30 percent. Three and four-bedroom rentals consequently gained ground. "When travel becomes everyday life, demand for kitchens, living rooms, multiple bedrooms and local experiences increases," said Hu Yang, Tujia's senior vice-president. The economics help explain the appeal. Staying longer spreads transport costs over more days; cooking and sharing accommodation can contain household spending. Ming Qingzhong, a professor at Yunnan University of Finance and Economics, said sojourn living shifts the spending mix toward local foods, accommodation and other everyday services. More of a visitor's budget can circulate in the destination's economy.

item.title: Xi's speech praised for future vision
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Xi's speech praised for future vision National Day address reflected China's journey, peaceful goals, observers say President Xi Jinping's speech, delivered on the eve of China's National Day on Oct 1, has been praised by observers as one that reflected both confidence in China's remarkable journey and a clear vision for its future, conveying a clear signal of the nation's unwavering commitment to global peace and development. Speaking at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Wednesday, Xi said that over the past 77 years, the Communist Party of China has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. On foreign affairs, Xi said China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it has proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world. Proposed by Xi between 2021 and 2025, the four major global initiatives on development, security, civilization and governance serve as China's public goods to advance global governance reform and build a community with a shared future for humanity. These themes resonated strongly with international observers, who underscored the global relevance of China's development trajectory. They lauded China's achievements in modernization over the past decades, emphasizing their significant relevance and lessons for a number of developing countries. Aruna Goonatilleke, president of the Sri Lanka-China Friendship Association, said President Xi's balanced assessment — combining grounded confidence in the country's vast economic growth and long-term social stability with a sober awareness of future challenges — demonstrates why China's governance model remains a beacon for developing nations. "As China transitions from achieving a moderately prosperous society to pursuing its second centenary goal of building a great modern socialist country, its steady progress proves that independent, socialist-led development offers a clear, proven path toward national dignity and prosperity," she said. "For Global South countries like Sri Lanka, China's growing strength is not merely an internal milestone, but a vital force for global stability, equity and peace," Goonatilleke said. "President Xi's reaffirmation of an independent foreign policy of peace, alongside China's commitment to advancing the four global initiatives and building a community with a shared future for humanity, brings much-needed certainty to today's volatile geopolitical landscape." Keith Bennett, senior international affairs analyst and co-editor of the Friends of Socialist China platform, echoed this view, noting that socialism with Chinese characteristics offers a new example for countries that wish to rapidly develop their economies while maintaining their independence. "In reaffirming that China will pursue an independent foreign policy of peace, Xi is making clear that China will strive to create the best possible conditions for the country's modernization and also at the same time work tirelessly toward the creation of a global community of shared future for humanity, and that these two goals cannot be separated from one another," Bennett said. David Tabacznyj, founder of France-based artificial intelligence training company allIAnce, said that modernization is not only about infrastructure, technology or economic growth; it is first about people and the opportunities created for them to improve their lives. "What impressed me most was the speed of change and the collective capacity to adapt in China," Tabacznyj said. "Chinese modernization should not be viewed in Europe only through competition. It can create bridges, cooperation and mutual understanding, which are essential for long-term global stability," he said. Observers also pointed to the evolving nature and international implications of China's development path. Tom Harper, a China specialist and lecturer in international relations at the University of East London, said the speech showed the priorities in China's development, which have been to pursue higher quality and more environmentally friendly growth. It is also indicative of the priorities for Chinese foreign policy in the near future, he added. Moiz Farooq, executive editor of Pakistan Economic Net and Daily Ittehad Media Group, said: "Equally significant is President Xi's message to the international community. His emphasis on peace, cooperation, the four global initiatives and building a community with a shared future for humanity reflects China's stated approach toward contributing greater stability and certainty to an increasingly complex international environment," Farooq said. Zhang Zhouxiang in Brussels, Xing Yi and Wang Mingjie in London contributed to this story. Contact the writers at vivienxu@chinadailyapac.com

item.title: Diving into the details: a chat with perfectionist Chen Yuxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Diving into the details: a chat with perfectionist Chen Yuxi Share - WeChat
Winning two gold medals at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, Chinese diving star Chen Yuxi continues to look beyond the podium. In an exclusive conversation with China Daily's online show Spotlight, Chen reflects on her Asian Games journey, the mindset behind each dive, and her constant pursuit of improvement. For Chen, diving is like polishing a piece of artwork — there is always something to refine, and every competition brings new experiences and challenges. More than a sport, diving has also become an inseparable part of her life. To find out more, click the video.
